Shows and controls in Gladys the devices of your **Hubspace** account (Home
Depot, Afero cloud): lights, plugs and switches, ceiling fans, bathroom
exhaust-fan sensors, and the state of locks and water timers.

> **Unofficial API, never tested with a real account.** The integration talks
> to the API of the Hubspace app, which Hubspace does not document and may
> change at any time. It was written from the aioafero library (the one of
> the Home Assistant integration) and tested with made-up answers only. Not
> affiliated with Hubspace, Home Depot or Afero.

## What you get

One Gladys device per supported Hubspace device:

| Hubspace device           | Gladys features                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Light, dimmer             | On/Off, Brightness, Colour temperature, Colour (as the bulb allows); one set per zone (e.g. `main` and `trim`) |
| Plug, switch, transformer | On/Off (one per outlet or zone), Power (W) when the device gives it                                            |
| Ceiling fan               | On/Off, Speed (%), Direction                                                                                   |
| Exhaust fan               | Motion, Humidity above the threshold (read only)                                                               |
| Lock                      | Lock state (read only), Lock and Unlock buttons, Battery                                                       |
| Water timer               | Watering per spigot (1 = open, read only), Open the valve and Close the valve buttons, Battery                 |

The light of a ceiling fan is a device of its own (as in the app). The other
Hubspace devices (thermostats, air conditioners, dehumidifiers, security
system) are not shown yet. Garage doors are not handled by aioafero: not
here either.

### Locks and valves: off by default

- **Locks**: the state is read only, the commands are buttons (never a
  switch: an "everything off" from Gladys, a voice assistant or a scene
  cannot reach them). **Lock** is always allowed; **Unlock** is refused while
  _Allow unlocking the locks from Gladys_ is off (the default).
- **Water timers**: **Open the valve** and **Close the valve** are refused
  while _Allow the water valves (timers) from Gladys_ is off (the default);
  the state is still shown.
- Before every lock or valve command, the integration reads the state again
  from Hubspace: nothing is sent when the device is offline, the state is
  unknown or the lock is moving, and nothing is sent again when the device
  already is in the wanted state. The decision is made on that read alone: a
  state it does not carry is unknown.

> **Plugs and switches** are switches for Gladys, so for an "everything off"
> of a scene or a voice assistant (Google Home, Alexa, HomeKit). Do not expose
> to a voice assistant, nor put in an "everything off" scene, a plug that
> powers a pump, a freezer, an aquarium or a medical device.

## Setup

1. In Gladys, install the **Hubspace** integration from the store.
2. Enter the **e-mail** and **password** of your Hubspace account (the ones
   of the app), then save: the integration signs in once. If the status says
   "Not signed in", click **Test the connection**.
3. If the status says a code was e-mailed, see below.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices.

The password field is a `secret` field: Gladys keeps it in its database (in
plain text, like every configuration value, and in its backups), never shows
it again, and the integration sends it only to the Hubspace sign-in page
(`accounts.hubspaceconnect.com`).

**The password is sent only on an action of yours**: a newly saved e-mail or
password, a click on _Test the connection_ or on _Send the verification
code_. Never at a start, a reconnection to Gladys nor during the reads: as
Hubspace may e-mail a code at every sign-in, you never get a code you did not
ask for. The rest of the time, the integration renews its session with its
refresh token; when Hubspace refuses it, it stops ("session expired", even
after a restart) and waits for your click on _Test the connection_.

### Verification code (by e-mail)

Hubspace may ask for a code sent by e-mail when signing in. Hubspace then
sends the code at the sign-in, the integration stops and the status says so:

1. Under **Verify the code**, type the code of the last Hubspace e-mail and
   click the button. "Code accepted" means connected.
2. No e-mail, or the code is too old (more than 10 minutes)? Click **Send the
   verification code**: the integration signs in again and Hubspace e-mails a
   new code (at most once a minute).

The session is then kept (in the integration's `/data`): no code at the next
restarts. The integration never signs in by itself: a code is sent only
after you saved or clicked, and the wait for the code is kept across a
restart.

## Refresh

Every device is read every **60 seconds** by default (30 to 60, _Refresh
interval_), in **one request**. A command is sent at once; the value
Hubspace confirms shows at once and is not undone by a read slightly behind
(15 seconds).

The commands of one device run one after the other. Gladys waits 5 seconds
for the answer to a command: when Hubspace is too slow, the integration
refuses the command **before sending it** rather than sending it after the
failure is shown. A command sent without an answer is reported "sent, without
confirmation: check the state", and the state is read again a few seconds
later (likewise after a lock or valve command).

## Troubleshooting

- **E-mail or password refused**: the integration stops and waits, even
  after a restart. Fix them, then save (or click _Test the connection_). It
  never signs in again by itself after a refusal.
- **Session refused**: the session is renewed once; refused again, the
  integration pauses and tries again after 1 hour, 6 hours, then every
  24 hours (kept across a restart), never sending the password again.
  _Test the connection_ tries at once.
- **Session expired** (refresh token refused) or **not signed in**: a stop
  until a click on _Test the connection_. A sign-in left without an answer
  is never sent again by itself.
- **Unknown sign-in page**: Hubspace asks for a step the integration does
  not know (accept terms, change the password…): sign in once in the app,
  then click _Test the connection_.
- **Too many requests (429)**: a pause of 1 minute to 6 hours (Hubspace's
  `Retry-After`, 10 minutes without it), for the reads, the commands and the
  buttons, kept across a restart or a reconnection to Gladys. **HTTP 403**
  from the sign-in page: one hour.
- **Hubspace unavailable (5xx, network)**: new tries after 1, 2, 5, 10, then
  every 15 minutes, never sooner than the interval.
- A device offline for Hubspace is shown "unreachable" on its card.

## Limits

- Unofficial API: Hubspace may change it, block it or ask for more checks.
- No live updates (the app's "Conclave" channel): one read every 30 to
  60 seconds.
- One Hubspace account per Gladys.
- No light effects, timers or settings (LEDs, sensitivity, speaker…) in this
  version.
- Never tested with a real account: please report what you see on the
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-hubspace/issues)
  (without your e-mail, password or codes).

## Privacy

The integration keeps in `/data/hubspace-state.json` (readable by its own
container only): the refresh token only (the short-lived access token stays
in memory) and the Afero account id, the account they belong to as a hash of
the e-mail, a sign-in waiting for its code (its cookies and parameters), when
a code was last requested, the end of a 429 pause and of a 403 pause, and a
stop (refused credentials, unknown sign-in page, session expired, code
awaited, session refused and its next try) tied to a salted fingerprint of
the e-mail and password. Neither the e-mail nor the
password. Nothing is sent anywhere but to Hubspace and Afero.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Hubspace te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Hubspace account | `section` | No | Shows the devices of your Hubspace account (Home Depot, Afero cloud) in Gladys: lights (on/off, brightness, colour temperature, colour), plugs and switches, ceiling fans (on/off, speed, direction), exhaust-fan sensors, and the state of locks and water timers (commands off by default). Enter the e-mail and password of the Hubspace app, save, then add the devices from the Discovery tab. If Hubspace e-mails you a code, type it with the buttons below. Read every 60 seconds. Unofficial API, never tested with a real account. Not affiliated with Hubspace, Home Depot or Afero. |
| Hubspace e-mail | `string` | Sí |  |
| Hubspace password | `secret` | Sí | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the Hubspace sign-in page (accounts.hubspaceconnect.com). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | Seconds between two reads of every device (30 to 60): one request each time. |
| Allow unlocking the locks from Gladys | `boolean` | No | Off by default: the "Unlock" button of a lock is refused. Locking is always allowed. |
| Allow the water valves (timers) from Gladys | `boolean` | No | Off by default: the "Open the valve" and "Close the valve" buttons of a water timer are refused; its state is still shown. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on. |

## Cómo instalar Hubspace en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Hubspace aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-hubspace:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-hubspace](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-hubspace).

Hubspace requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Hubspace es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
